interest: This file provides valuable historical insight into the legal, economic, and administrative complexities surrounding private property and technology transfer during the Allied occupation of Japan. It illustrates the gradual evolution of American occupation policy from early postwar trade embargoes and reparations planning in 1946 under the Far Eastern Commission toward economic rehabilitation, intellectual property restoration, and commercial engagement by 1948. Furthermore, the 1948 correspondence provides a compelling case study of technology transfer in the nutritional and chemical sectors, showing how Japanese enterprises sought advanced American industrial know-how—specifically molecular distillation for vitamin extraction to combat postwar malnutrition—with the direct facilitation of SCAP's Economic and Scientific Section, while American corporations navigated patent security and wartime asset restoration under the guidance of key State Department officials such as Raymond Vernon.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP)
overview: This file (decimal file 894.54211, File 1653) from the U.S. State Department's central decimal files covers diplomatic and administrative correspondence from 1946 and 1948 concerning the postwar status, restoration, and protection of American intellectual and industrial property rights in Allied-occupied Japan. The documentation centers on two primary inquiries: a March 1946 exchange initiated by international patent firm Marks & Clerk regarding the reinstatement of lapsed patents and trademarks and the safeguarding of American-owned subsidiary manufacturing plants under SCAP jurisdiction; and an August–September 1948 exchange involving Distillation Products, Inc. regarding patent protection, royalties, and commercial vetting after receiving an inquiry from a Japanese chemical firm (Matsumoto Fat, Oil, & Chemical Man. Co. Ltd., recommended by SCAP's Economic and Scientific Section) seeking molecular distillation equipment and know-how to extract vitamins A and D from cod liver oil. Across these communications, State Department officials (including Robert P. Terrill, Roswell H. Whitman, and Raymond Vernon) clarify the transition from wartime sequestration and commercial prohibitions to Allied policies under the Far Eastern Commission and SCAP, outlining procedures for patent re-validation, war damage claims, and commercial intelligence channels.

subfiles.about: Preliminary acknowledgement of an inquiry regarding the status of American patents, trade-marks, and industrial property in occupied Japan.
subfiles.from: Robert P. Terrill, Assistant Chief, International Resources Division, Department of State
subfiles.summary: The Department of State acknowledges receipt of Marks and Clerk's letter dated March 15, 1946, concerning American patents, trade-marks, and other industrial property in Japan. The communication informs the patent firm that their letter is being given consideration. A substantive reply is promised in the near future.
subfiles.title: Letter from Robert P. Terrill to Marks and Clerk acknowledging inquiry on industrial property in Japan

subfiles.about: Inquiry by an international patent firm regarding the restoration of lapsed American patent and trademark rights and the disposition of American-owned manufacturing plants in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Marks & Clerk writes to the Department of State on behalf of American corporate clients regarding the postwar status of their patents and trade mark rights in Japan. The firm notes that communication with former Japanese associates is barred without Treasury Department licenses and asks whether arrangements are being made to reinstate lapsed rights. Furthermore, they inquire whether American subsidiary manufacturing plants in Japan have been vested in U.S. government agencies and whether compensation will be provided for the use of plant facilities.
subfiles.title: Letter from Marks & Clerk to the Department of State regarding patent rights and corporate property in Japan

subfiles.about: Detailed response outlining U.S. and Allied policy on American-owned patents, trade-marks, and physical assets in occupied Japan.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Acting Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Acting Chief Roswell H. Whitman replies to Marks and Clerk's March 15 inquiry, explaining that Japanese patent policy is under active inter-Allied consideration within the Far Eastern Commission. He confirms that private business communications remain prohibited because Japan is still classified as an enemy nation, though future reinstatement of patent rights may be permitted under general Japanese patent regulations. He also clarifies that foreign-owned physical property has not been vested in occupation forces, that SCAP has placed responsibility on the Japanese Government for safeguarding it, and that losses can be submitted as war damage claims toward overall reparations.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roswell H. Whitman to Marks and Clerk regarding Allied patent policy and property safeguarding in Japan

subfiles.about: Inquiry concerning patent protection, royalties, and commercial vetting following a request from a Japanese company for molecular distillation technology.
subfiles.from: R. W. Albright, General Manager, Distillation Products, Inc.
keywords: Matsumoto Fat, Oil, & Chemical Man. Co. Ltd.
subfiles.summary: Distillation Products, Inc. forwards an inquiry from Matsumoto Fat, Oil, & Chemical Man. Co. Ltd. requesting technical specifications and equipment for concentrating vitamin A from cod liver oil by molecular distillation. Albright asks whether American-owned patents are recognized in Japan or whether American companies are expected to furnish equipment and technical know-how without royalty returns or patent protection. He additionally requests State Department guidance on how to determine the commercial responsibility and standing of the inquiring Japanese firm.
subfiles.title: Letter from Distillation Products, Inc. to Department of State inquiring on patent protection and licensing in Japan

subfiles.about: Proposal by a Japanese chemical company to acquire molecular distillation apparatus and technical know-how to extract vitamins A and D from cod liver oil.
subfiles.from: Yuichi Shinozaki, Director, Matsumoto Fat, Oil, & Chemical Man. Co. Ltd.
keywords: Matsumoto Fat, Oil, & Chemical Man. Co. Ltd.
subfiles.summary: Writing upon the recommendation of GHQ-SCAP's Economic and Scientific Section (Scientific and Technical Division), Director Yuichi Shinozaki solicits technical data and plant equipment from Distillation Products, Inc. He explains that postwar nutritional shortages in Japan necessitate large-scale extraction of vitamins A and D from cod liver oil via molecular distillation. He outlines plant requirements for centrifugal stills treating up to two tons daily, offers to enter into formal contracts, and expresses high admiration for the pioneering research of Dr. Hickman.
subfiles.title: Letter from Yuichi Shinozaki of Matsumoto Fat, Oil, & Chemical Man. Co. Ltd. to Distillation Products, Inc.

subfiles.about: State Department guidance on upcoming procedures for restoring American patent rights in Japan and vetting Japanese business partners.
subfiles.from: Raymond Vernon, Assistant Chief, International Resources Division, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Raymond Vernon explains that although American patents in Japan were seized under wartime legislation or lapsed for non-payment of fees, plans are underway to permit foreign nationals to apply for restoration and re-validation before the end of 1948. He assures Distillation Products, Inc. that the U.S. Government intends to ensure that American patent rights will be enforceable in Japan. Regarding the commercial vetting of Matsumoto Fat, Oil, & Chemical Man. Co. Ltd., Vernon advises Albright to direct inquiries to Frank Pickelle, Chief of the Foreign Trade Division of SCAP's Economic and Scientific Section in Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Letter from Raymond Vernon to Distillation Products, Inc. regarding patent restoration and commercial intelligence in Japan
subfiles.to: R. W. Albright, General Manager, Distillation Products, Inc.
